title: POC Weekly Sync - Reliability Incident Follow-up
summary: Weekly POC sync to review last week's reliability incident (timeouts and 5xxs), triage root causes, tuning recommendations (retries, backoff, rate limits, batching), and agree next steps for extended testing and security docs. AE + SE on call; customer SRE and security present. Agreed to run a 24h load test, share logs, and provide security packet and pricing for Dedicated config.
next_steps: Marcus to run 24h extended load test simulating peak traffic and provide results by 2026-05-28
Liam to send log slices (request IDs) from 2026-05-22 incident to Marcus by EOD 2026-05-25
Ava to share Dedicated pricing and recommended capacity plan (gpus + burst) by 2026-05-26
Sofia and Redwood security to set up a follow-up review of SOC2 artifacts and KMS integration on 2026-05-27
Team to schedule canary rollout of updated retry/backoff policy next week (tentative 2026-06-01)
action_items: Marcus (Redwood SE): run extended load test w/ client traffic profile; due 2026-05-28
Liam (FinWave SRE): export and share 5xx/timeout request IDs and traces; due 2026-05-25
Ava (Redwood AE): send Dedicated/Private pricing + config notes and link to benchmark sheet; due 2026-05-26
Sofia (FinWave Sec): confirm specific KMS/HSM vendor questions and provide compliance checklist; due 2026-05-27
transcript:
[00:00] Ava (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining - we tried to keep this tight, 45 minutes. Quick roll call?
[00:08] Jenna (FinWave Eng Manager): hi yeah Jenna here.
[00:11] Liam (FinWave SRE): Liam on SRE.
[00:13] Sofia (FinWave Security): Sofia from security.
[00:15] Marcus (Redwood SE): Marcus here, Redwood SE.
[00:18] Tom (FinWave PM): Tom here.
[00:20] Ava: Cool. Quick context: last week you hit a spike of 5xxs and client timeouts around 3pm PDT on Friday, correct? Wanted to go through our findings and the plan.
[00:32] Jenna: yep that's right, we saw a bunch of timeouts in the app, users reported degraded latency and a few 502/503s.
[00:38] Liam: to add - our sidecar had retries turned on but we started seeing request storms and retries amplifying load. So we ended up throttling client side which reduced availability.
[00:50] Marcus: right, thanks. We pulled initial traces and saw two patterns: one was upstream resource pressure on the model-serving pods leading to queueing; second was transient 5xx from a GPU node that started OOMing under a larger batch size.
[01:05] Ava: and I think there was a config mix - you were testing higher batching sizes for cost optimization?
[01:10] Tom: yeah we were trying to push batch size to save tokens/cost, but maybe we overdid it. We have a spreadsheet link in the deck (shared) - quick note we changed quantization too in one branch.
[01:22] Jenna: also important: a deploy happened around the same time, but not sure if related.
[01:27] Marcus: ok good. So root cause hypothesis: (1) aggressive batching + quant so kernel memory bumped, caused eviction/5xx on a subset of nodes, (2) retries w/o jitter amplified the traffic, (3) rate limit thresholds were hit and the fallback path wasn't graceful.
[01:42] Liam: that aligns. We traced ~12% of requests hitting 5xx and timeouts spiked to 7% for a period ~10m. Users saw errors.
[01:51] Sofia: from security perspective we also want to confirm there was no exfil or anything - logs show nothing but we'll want the audit logs and request IDs.
[01:58] Ava: we'll definitely share the request IDs + a log slice. Marcus, can you talk through immediate config changes we recommend?
[02:05] Marcus: sure. Short list: reduce batch size on the problematic model variant by 25%, enable KV prefix cache for hot prefixes to avoid re-computing full context, and implement conservative client-side retry with exponential backoff + jitter and a short circuit breaker after N fails. Also enable per-route rate limiting and token bucket with burst window.
[02:27] Liam: can you clarify the circuit breaker thresholds? We want to avoid cutting into normal traffic but also dampen storms.
[02:33] Marcus: recommend: fail-open for low severity, but set breaker to trip when error rate > 5% over 30s and min requests 100, then cool down 60s with linear backoff. But this is tunable - we can give a config to simulate.
[02:50] Jenna: is that default in Redwood Console or do we need to patch our sidecar?
[02:55] Marcus: Console has rate limit and policy primitives; for client retry you control via the SDK or our gateway. For now I'd recommend server-side protections in Console plus client changes.
[03:07] Ava: important tradeoff note - adding aggressive rate limiting reduces error blast but could increase tail latency for some legitimate requests; we need to decide SLO priorities.
[03:18] Tom: our priority is availability for critical flows, user-facing chat should degrade gracefully. Cost less important during the pilot.
[03:25] Marcus: good to hear. On Dedicated vs Hosted: if you move to Dedicated, we can reserve capacity and reduce noisy neighbor risk. But Dedicated won't magically fix mis-configured retries. It does give predictable throughput and isolation - recommended if you expect sustained peak.
[03:40] Liam: what about Private (VPC) option? We have compliance constraints and prefer traffic not transit public internet for some subsets.
[03:46] Ava: Redwood Private supports VPC and on-prem; security will want SOC2 docs + KMS integration. Sofia, did you have specifics?
[03:54] Sofia: mainly KMS/HSM vendor compatibility, audit log retention, and admin RBAC. Also we need to know latency to our region, and whether Dedicated can be colocated in region.
[04:05] Marcus: we'll include KMS integration notes and expected latencies. For the incident we saw network jitter as a minor factor but not primary.
[04:13] Jenna: can we get a ballpark on Dedicated pricing for the capacity you'd recommend?
[04:18] Ava: yes we'll send a recommended config - starting point: 4 dedicated gpus with burst pool of 1-2; pricing in the email. We'll attach the benchmark sheet.
[04:28] Liam: Marcus, you mentioned KV cache - how much headroom do we need in RAM to enable it? We run medium length contexts ~1k tokens on average.
[04:36] Marcus: for context ~1k tokens, enabling prefix KV cache reduces decode compute by ~20-30% and memory increase is modest per-gpu (a few GB) depending on kv chunking. We'll provide numbers per model variant in the doc.
[04:50] Ava: ok let's go into the timeline of what happened - Liam can you summarize the Friday spike?
[04:55] Liam: sure. At 14:58 PDT we saw a usage burst due to a marketing campaign. Our gateway retried some 429s aggressively; the client retry policy was exponential without jitter which caused synchronized retries; at the same time a deploy increased batch size on staging->prod by mistake for that model variant, pushing few nodes into OOM and 5xxing. The combination amplified load and triggered secondary throttles.
[05:22] Marcus: thanks. Two parallel mitigations: (1) rollback the batch change - you already did that, right?
[05:27] Jenna: yes we rolled back within 8 minutes.
[05:29] Marcus: (2) adjust retry policy and add circuit breaker - we deployed a short-lived gate but want to formalize it.
[05:36] Tom: question - why did OOM happen only on subset of nodes?
[05:39] Marcus: likely a kernel selection/quantization path difference; some nodes fell into a slower kernel path that used more memory under larger batch sizes - small variance in model shards. We'll run diagnostics.
[05:50] Liam: we also saw CPU load spike on the control plane during the event - API gateway queued requests which increased end-to-end latency.
[05:57] Ava: ok good. For the extended tests - Marcus, can you outline the load test you'll run?
[06:02] Marcus: yes. We'll run 24h test that reproduces FinWave's traffic shape: baseline 120rps with 30 minute peak of 600rps every 4 hours, plus bursty tail; we'll simulate client retry behaviors both naive and with recommended backoff. We'll monitor 5xx, p95/p99 latency, OOMs, and kernel path variance.
[06:22] Jenna: please include a run that exercises quantized model variant vs baseline so we can see memory differences.
[06:27] Marcus: will do. We'll share a result spreadsheet and traces.
[06:30] Sofia: on security artifacts - we'll need the SOC2 type 2 report, encryption in transit + at rest docs, KMS integration doc, and RBAC admin guide.
[06:39] Ava: noted, I'll share the security packet link (security_packet_redwood.pdf) and set up a follow-up to walk through specifics.
[06:45] Tom: can we get the exact request IDs and traces from the 5xx window? That'll help our internal blamestorm.
[06:51] Liam: yes we'll export and send them to Marcus by tomorrow.
[06:54] Marcus: great. A note on rate limits: we recommend a token-bucket per-tenant with a burst window and a slow-start throttle to avoid synchronized bursts. Also server-side pre-emptive rejects with Retry-After headers help clients back off properly.
[07:12] Jenna: what about SDK behavior - if we add Retry-After header, does the SDK automatically honor it?
[07:18] Marcus: our Redwood SDK supports honoring Retry-After by default in recent versions; if you're on older SDK we'll send a patch.
[07:24] Ava: anything else from security?
[07:26] Sofia: also please confirm audit log retention configurable to 13 months for our compliance.
[07:31] Ava: yes that's configurable with the enterprise package.
[07:34] Marcus: small implementation detail - we'll instrument client-side jitter to be randomized between 0.5x and 1.5x the backoff interval to avoid sync.
[07:43] Tom: sweet. Ok so practical actions and timeline?
[07:47] Ava: recap: Marcus runs load test and shares results by 05-28; Liam sends logs by 05-25; Ava sends pricing and security packet links by 05-26; follow-up security deep-dive on 05-27. Also we plan canary rollout of new retry policy next week.
[08:03] Jenna: that sounds good.
[08:05] Liam: one more operational ask - can Redwood expose per-route tokens and request tracing in Console for easier debugging?
[08:11] Marcus: yes Console shows per-route token consumption and tracing; we'll add the relevant dashboard to your org and give you viewer access.
[08:20] Sofia: when you say dedicated gpus, what GPU family? A100? V100? We need perf numbers per-instance.
[08:27] Ava: recommended is A100 or H100 depending on model; Marcus will include perf numbers per gpu family in the benchmark sheet.
[08:36] Marcus: note: with quantization we can run on T4-like class for lower perf but much cheaper; we'll quantify latency/cost.
[08:45] Jenna: ok good. Any blockers to start the extended test?
[08:49] Marcus: need the exact traffic profile and sample traces - Liam said he'll send those. Also need a short window to coordinate config change to mirror production.
[08:58] Liam: sending now after this call.
[09:00] Ava: great. Let's do a quick Q&A and then finish.
[09:05] Tom: Q: if we go Dedicated, what's the expected RTO/RPO for failover?
[09:10] Marcus: with Dedicated plus cross-region fallback we can target RTO ~30s for short outages and RPO near zero for request retries, but we need to provision a warm standby region for that. We'll outline tradeoffs in the config doc.
[09:24] Sofia: Q: KMS integration latency - will using external KMS add noticeable token latency?
[09:29] Marcus: slightly on cold start for key fetches, but we cache keys and keep latency minimal; we'll provide numbers.
[09:36] Jenna: small nit - our SLO for chat p95 is 600ms. If we add circuit breaker, p95 may shift, will that be acceptable?
[09:44] Ava: we should aim to maintain p95 for successful requests; circuit breakers primarily reduce error amplification not latency for successful calls.
[09:52] Marcus: right; with KV cache+p95 tuning we should improve p95 for most flows.
[09:58] Ava: ok that wraps it. Any other items?
[10:01] Jenna: none.
[10:03] Liam: none.
[10:05] Sofia: none.
[10:07] Ava: thanks everyone. We'll follow up with notes, pricing, and the security packet. Marcus will kick off the 24h load test.
[10:15] Tom: thanks all.
[10:18] (call ends)

Notes on transcript quality: auto transcription; some names/terms may be mis-heard (RedWood Privat -> Redwood Private, KV-cache spelled variably). Shared artifacts referenced: security_packet_redwood.pdf (link to be sent), benchmark_sheet_finwave.xlsx (shared), incident_log_slice_20260522.zip (to be shared).
